title: Kerusi State
description: A complete per-seat availability and hold snapshot for a session or map (Kerusi v1.0, RFC section 5.1).

kerusi.description: Spec version this document conforms to (section 7).

sessionId.description: Matches KerusiSession.id. RECOMMENDED when the referenced map is reused across many events (section 5.3).

mapId.description: Matches KerusiMap.id directly, for documents with no separate session concept.

updatedAt.$comment: Deliberate narrowing: 'format: date-time' is the RFC 3339 profile of ISO 8601, not all of ISO 8601. It rejects forms the spec's phrase 'ISO 8601' admits - '2026-08-17T09:14Z' (seconds omitted) and the basic format '20260817T091400Z' - and, per RFC 3339 section 5.6, some validators also accept a space in place of 'T'. RFC 3339 is what interoperating producers mean in practice, so this schema requires it; the spec text should say so explicitly before 1.0 is declared stable.

seats.description: Keyed by Seat.id. Sparse: a seat absent from this object MUST be interpreted as { "status": "available" } (section 5.1).
seats.$comment: Every key MUST match a Seat.id in the referenced KerusiMap (section 3, merge by Seat.id). Cross-document reference; enforce with a custom validator holding both the map and this state. The sparse default is a semantic rule for consumers and needs no schema enforcement - an empty seats object is a valid, fully-available snapshot.

allOf.title: Session-or-map scope (section 5.1)
allOf.description: Exactly one of sessionId or mapId MUST be present.

status.description: 'blocked' denotes a seat withheld from sale by the venue, distinct from 'booked' (sold) and 'held' (temporarily reserved during checkout).

holdExpires.description: ISO 8601. Meaningful only when status is 'held'.
holdExpires.$comment: Section 5.1 makes holdExpires meaningful only for 'held' but does not forbid it elsewhere, so this schema does not reject it on another status. Hold duration, extension, queueing, and race resolution are explicitly out of scope. Deliberate narrowing: 'format: date-time' is the RFC 3339 profile of ISO 8601, not all of ISO 8601. RFC 3339 is what interoperating producers mean in practice, so this schema requires it; the spec text should say so explicitly before 1.0 is declared stable.
